content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes normalizing the activation functions in feedforward neural networks so as to regularize the gradients for efficient training. The normalization method is an affine transformation, whose parameters are determined by forcing the second moments of the function and its derivative to be one. Compared to the previous methods which fix the affine transformation parameters (under the Gaussian assumption), this work allows them to be adaptive during training using mini-batch statistics.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. The paper is well-written and easy to follow. 
2. The idea is well-motivated: previous works such as Dynamical Isometry and Bidirectionally Self-Normalizing Neural Networks only consider regularizing the gradient at initialization, this work tries to keep the normalization properties throughout training.
3. Experiments were carried out on various activation functions and datasets.

Weaknesses:
1. The updating procedure (16)-(18) is ad hoc. This is no justification on how or under what conditions the procedure can ensure the normalization properties preserved during training. Besides, it is problematic to disable the backward gradient of the normalization parameters. For a comparison, note that BatchNorm does backprop the gradient to work well.
2. The experiments are insufficient to support the effective of the proposed method. There is no significant speed-up of the proposed method in terms of test accuracy vs epochs.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper has good clarity. The novelty is marginal. The code is attached and seems reproducible.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper combines affine transformation of activation functions with moving average update of the parameters. I find the paper lacks of theoretically, technically and empirically significance.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper proposes a new framework to normalize activation functions, with the goal of retaining the variance of the gradient to better achieve convergence during optimization.

The authors follow the derivation from Glorot (2010) and introduce a scaling step to normalize and keep the variance approximately the same on each layer. To this end, the authors introduce a wrapper over standard activation functions that centers and scales the outputs of the activation function.

The authors then present an empirical evaluation of their approach showing higher validation accuracy.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The authors start from a nice theoretical foundation. However, they then proceed with their contributions making changes along the way that are neither backed by theory, nor experiments, and they make no further comments. One such example is the introduction of a dampening parameter in the form of $0.3\tanh\left(\alpha\right)$. 

There is another confusing aspect, you introduce $\rho_n$ in eq. 5, but in Fig. 1, it seems to be computed in a different way.

The empirical evaluation does not provide a good ablation study of your contributions (more details on the summary).
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The language could be improved in some places (e.g., "testify", "we can make it more satisfy", etc.). My score however does not take this into account.

The difference in the already mentioned $\rho_n$ causes some confusion when we are interested in understanding and implementing the approach.

Readers would appreciate some more words on eq. 13, what are the benefits? disadvantages?.
content.summary_of_the_review:
The paper introduces an interesting approach to normalization. The main weakness is the empirical evaluation, where it is hard to distinguish what made the approach work or the effect of each of the components, or whether it is necessary to combine it with BN to obtain good results.

There is no mention of the computational cost, this can be evaluated by comparing the time per epoch of the different approaches. Is your normalization more expensive to compute? and if so, are the improvements per epoch still advantageous when comparing against time?

To provide more details on the empirical evaluation, one could argue that batch-norm or other layer normalization techniques would be more appropriate baselines to compare against. Given that normalization layers, are usually defined by centering and scale operations, the empirical evaluation of your contribution should focus on showing how your scale operation offers clear benefits.

In the same way, some experiments on the momentum approach would be valuable. Again, we are interested in finding out what is the impact of the different aspects of your contribution to the different goals (e.g., accuracy, convergence).

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a new operation, which can be used after each activation function in a neural network. This operation is meant to help training by normalizing the output of an activation function, in such a way that the variance of the activations and the variance of the backpropagated gradients are preserved. This operation is broadly inspired by Xavier initialization.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strengths

Impossible to evaluate. See below.

## Weaknesses

### Previous works

The authors seem to ignore many works that have been done since Glorot [A]. For instance, He [B] has been cited, but the authors seem to ignore that, when looking for a good value for $\mathrm{Var}(W)$, it is not necessary to use the (inverse) arithmetical mean (see Eqn. (4)) proposed by Glorot (that is, $2/(n_l + n_{l + 1}$), it is sufficient to choose either $1/n_l$ or $1/n_{l + 1}$, where $n_l$ is the dimension of the input of layer $l$.

In the same way, works about the Edge of Chaos [C,D] are not cited, though they contribute to understand how to make information propagate and backpropagate properly.

### Comparison to BatchNorm

The authors do not compare their technique to BatchNorm, though they are very close to each other. They only indicate how to combine the two techniques.

Without this comparison, it is impossible for the reader to have a clear idea of the performance of the proposed method.


[A] *Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural networks*, Glorot and Bengio, 2010.

[B] *Delving deep into rectifiers: Surpassing human-level performance on imagenet classification*, He et al., 2015.

[C] *Exponential expressivity in deep neural networks through transient chaos*, Poole et al., 2016.

[D] *Deep information propagation*, Schoenholz et al., 2016.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
## Clarity

The clarity of the paper can be improved:
* after Eqn. (12), there is a meaningless sentence: "Since $\rho_i$ and $\rho_i'$ given an activation function $\delta_i$ can be calculated";
* section 3.3, 2nd paragraph, very long sentence, almost impossible to understand: "we replaced all activation functions which is not following the element-wise addition in the bottleneck with their normalized version [...]" (5 lines long!); 
* it is not necessary to give a number to each equation;
* when making a reference to an equation, it is preferable to put the equation number into parentheses, which can be done by using "$\backslash$eqref\{ref_to_eqn\}";
* straight letters: Eqn. (6): use strait letters "d" into the derivative; prefer "$\mathrm{Cost}$" to "$Cost$" (even better: use only one letter to represent the cost function, such as "$C$", "$L$" or "$\ell$"); idem with the "$Score$" in Eqn. (22)
* Eqn. (21): adapt the size of the parentheses.

## Quality

Without comparison between the proposed method and BatchNorm, it is impossible to evaluate its effectiveness.

## Novelty

The lack of comparison between other techniques related to the initial idea of the authors (BatchNorm, improving propagation and backpropagation, e.g., Edge of Chaos line of works [C] [D]) prevents the reader to evaluate fairly the novelty of the proposed method.

## Reproducibility

No major issue related to reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: The lack of discussion about papers with similar ideas and the absence of empirical comparison with BatchNorm are two major issues. Therefore, it is impossible for the reader to check whether the proposed method is well-founded and efficient.

content.title: Thank you for suggestions and the critical reading.
content.comment:
Thank you for suggestions and the critical reading.

**The authors seem to ignore many works that have been done since Glorot [A].**
For all experiments, we use PyTorch where the implementation of Xavier initialization is using the inverse arithmetical mean. Our paper is consistent to this and this has no negative effect, typically when layers are far from being square.

**In the same way, works about the Edge of Chaos [C,D] are not cited**

Thank you for the constructive comment. We are rewriting part of our paper and will add *related works* section to cover broader survey including the Edge of Chaos line of works.

**Comparison to BatchNorm**

+ Our method and BatchNorm are not exclusive. It would be necessary to compare, if they were exclusive. 
+ Though our method and BatchNorm consist of shifting and scaling ops, the purposes of them are different. Our method recovers the variance of forward signal and normalizes the backprop signal. Therefore, we choose the GPN activation function which normalizes the signals bidirectionally as the baseline. However, their method are incompatible with residual networks. It prevent us to run more comparative experiments.
+ One merit of our method is simple and quick to improve existing models using kinds of architectures. Therefore, we have paid much attention to its compatibility with other existing techniques.

**Clarity**

Thank you for the comment. We are rewriting part of paper and will carefully proofread.

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper studies the relation between activation functions and the variance of the gradients. Consequently, it proposes an approach to normalize the activation functions (with focus on ReLU and Swish) aiming to improve convergence speed.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
* the topic addressed is timely and a good understanding of it may ensure in the future an increased performance for deep learning models
* the empirical validation performed shows that the proposed normalization method applied to Swish and ReLU can slightly improve the accuracy over their non-normalized baselines 

Weaknesses:
* the paper has a relatively small level of novelty
* the reported performance in terms of accuracy for all models seems quite small with several percentages less than what it is typically reported in the literature for that particular combination model-dataset. For instance, VGG-19/CIFAR100 reaches just around 64-65% accuracy, while usually it can be easily around 70%. Is this an effect yielded by the removal of Batch Normalization? If so, a good empirical evaluation for the CNN models would require also the Batch Normalization to be included systematically in the comparisons. I am not usually looking up to the "highest" number, but in this case the reported performance values seem too low and may hinder a good evaluation/understanding of the proposed methodology behaviour.
* the proposed methodology is not easy to follow and understand. Please try to clarify its presentation style using a more systematic approach. Adding some diagrams/plots to illustrate visually how NSwish and NReLU works in comparison with Swish and ReLU may help, but it would not be sufficient.
* the related work can be improved to make more clear the contributions of this paper. It seems that currently it is missing some related research which could be used also as a baseline (e.g., [1]).
* minor: the paper requires a careful proofread to improve the overall presentation and English usage. For instance, it has typos (e.g., “…However, We would…”)

Reference:

[1] Richemond and Guo, Static Activation Function Normalization, 2019
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: The paper would benefit by redesigning/rewriting in a more systematic manner some parts of it (particularly, the proposed methodology section) to increase readability. Also, a thorough proofread is necessary. Section 4 (Discussion) and Section 5 (Conclusion) could be extended with more qualitative discussions about the results obtained, but also about the limitations of the work.

Quality: The paper seem to have a fair quality level, but some aspects of it needs improvement. Particularly, the design of the empirical validation requires some adjustments to be more comprehensive and to support better the paper claims.

Originality: Related work could be extended to cover a broader literature survey. This would also help to make more sharp clear the paper contributions. Currently, there is no separate "Related Work and Background" section.

Reproducibility: The author provides some files just with the code of NSwish and NReLU. This is very appreciated, but a bit incomplete. In addition, it would be useful to provide a complete prototype code (which can be run at a click distance) together with a readme file to ease the reader job when trying out the proposed methodology.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper presents an interesting approach to tackle the normalisation of activation function. While promising, in my opinion, the paper seems to be immature enough and not ready yet for publication.

content.title: Thank you for the appreciation
content.comment:
We thank the reviewer for the appreciation of our work and the inspiring comments

**1. the reported performance in terms of accuracy for all models seems quite small with several percentages less than what it is typically reported in the literature for that particular combination model-dataset.**

It is because we didn’t add any learning rate scheduler in the experiments on VGG and ResNet. We find that using different learning rate schedulers may cause slightly different result when we want to compare ReLU and NReLU on VGG. In order to avoid extra discussion on learning rate scheduler, we didn’t use any learning rate scheduler here. Besides, Batch Normalization is kept in experiments.

**2. the proposed methodology is not easy to follow and understand.**

It is a great advice. We are rewriting our paper in a more systematic way. We will add the separate *related works* section and extent more discussions. And we will carefully proofread the paper. 

**3. the related work can be improved to make more clear the contributions of this paper.**

Thank you for the inspiring advice. We are adding related work section and cover a broader survey. Currently, we choose GPN activation function as the baseline. GPN activation function is to normalize signals bidirectionally by scaling and shifting the post-activation, which is similar to our work. However, their work, like some other related works, restricts the architecture of models, to be a FFN here. Therefore, it prohibits us to carry on the experiments comparing them on ResNet or with BN. Actually, it indicates one of the merits of our method. Our method is simple and quick to improve kinds of existing models, in spite of their different architectures in some way.

We would like to open source of training code with a readme file in future.
